name: Photosensitive Occipital Lobe Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Photosensitive Occipital Lobe Epilepsy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of occipital lobe seizure semiology including visual symptoms such as visual hallucinations or blindness
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing photoparoxysmal response to intermittent photic stimulation
Ictal EEG demonstrating seizure onset localized to the occipital lobe
Exclusion of other epilepsy syndromes and structural lesions by clinical and imaging evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical occipital seizure semiology, photoparoxysmal EEG response, and ictal occipital EEG focus) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical features with EEG findings; MRI is typically normal or shows no epileptogenic lesion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visual hallucinations with colored or geometric patterns
searchTerms: seeing colored or geometric visual hallucinations
visual hallucinations with patterns or colors
seeing shapes or colors not real

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient homonymous hemianopsia or visual field deficits during seizures
searchTerms: temporary loss of half visual field during seizures
transient visual field defects with seizures
partial vision loss during seizure episodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Photoparoxysmal EEG response triggered by intermittent photic stimulation
searchTerms: brain wave response triggered by light flashes

common.symptomName: Ictal blindness or transient loss of vision
searchTerms: loss of vision during seizure episodes

common.symptomName: Brief tonic or clonic eye movements
searchTerms: short tonic or clonic eye spasms

occasional.symptomName: Nausea or vomiting during or after seizures
Autonomic symptoms such as pallor or sweating
searchTerms: autonomic symptoms like pale skin or sweating

rare.symptomName: Secondary generalized tonic-clonic seizures without photic trigger
searchTerms: tonic-clonic seizures not caused by photosensitivity

rare.symptomName: Visual aura with scotomas or flashing lights
searchTerms: visual aura with flashing lights or blind spots
seeing scotomas or flashing before headache

imaging: Normal brain MRI or nonspecific occipital lobe changes
EEG showing photoparoxysmal response and occipital epileptiform discharges
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; possible familial predisposition to photosensitive epilepsy
other: Seizures triggered by flickering lights or visual stimuli

distinguishingFeatures: Myoclonic jerks predominantly in the morning
Generalized spike-and-wave EEG pattern without occipital focus
Lack of isolated occipital visual symptoms
Seizures not triggered by visual stimuli

redFlags: Sudden onset of persistent visual loss not resolving postictally
Seizures refractory to standard antiepileptic drugs
Development of focal neurological deficits or cognitive decline
references: Panayiotopoulos CP. The Epilepsies: Seizures, Syndromes and Management. Oxford University Press; 2010.
Kasteleijn-Nolst Trenité DG, et al. Photosensitive epilepsy: a review and practical guide. Epilepsia. 2012.
Orphanet Report: Photosensitive Occipital Lobe Epilepsy ORPHA:166409.
